title: Thousands rally at parliament in Lisbon over housing crisis
seoTitle: Lisbon housing crisis protest at parliament

tea.why: Protesters demonstrated against a worsening home affordability crisis, stagnant wages, and recent police operations against activists.
tea.want: Protesters demanded an end to rent caps removal on new leases, the scrapping of a bill speeding up evictions, and affordable housing.
tea.changed: Oct 28: Protests slowed down at the parliament and were set to return to Rossio.

summary: Thousands of people gathered outside the Portuguese parliament in Lisbon on Tuesday to protest against a severe housing crisis and recent police actions against housing activists, coinciding with lawmakers debating the 2027 draft budget. The demonstration followed weekend police operations that dismantled tent camps in Lisbon and Porto using baton charges, triggering accusations of excessive force and official inquiries. Organisers stated that several thousand people participated in the rally. Protesters demanded the government scrap legislation easing evictions and removing rent caps on new leases, while also calling for the protection of the right to protest. Prime Minister Luis Montenegro defended the police actions in parliament, stating they complied with principles of necessity and proportionality.
demands: Scrap the bill speeding up evictions
End rent caps on new leases
Ensure decent and affordable housing for everyone
response: Prime Minister Luis Montenegro stated in parliament that police acted proportionally and adequately. The internal affairs watchdog (IGAI) opened an inquiry and prosecutors launched a separate investigation into officer conduct.
